newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Borsodchem exports up 12.1 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Borsodchem exports up 12.1 pct in 1996.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem Rt 's exports rose 12.1 percent in forint terms in 1996 and the company met most of its goals for the last year, the company said in its earnings report on Friday.
"The company has achieved its main 1996 targets of maintaining cost-competitiveness and improving productivity," it said.

Borsodchem posted a HAS consolidated, not audited net profit of 5.80 billion forints on net sales of 43.65 billion forints versus 6.09 billion forints net profit on net sales of 41.34 billion in 1995. The company added that it expects IAS figures to be better than the HAS ones.
Exports totalled 27 billion forints in 1996 against 24.09 billion in 1995, and accounted for 62 percent of Borsodchem's total sales, it said.
It added that 56 percent of the exports went to western Europe, 35 percent to central and east European countries, five percent to the Far East and four percent to other markets.

In 1996 Borsodchem spent three billion forints on capacity increase, boosting its MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) capacity to 250,000 tonnes per year from 210,000 tonnes per year and its PVC production capacity to 32,500 tonnes per year from 25,000 tonnes.

The average international market price of Borsodchem's main product, PVC powder, dropped 28 percent in 1996 from 1995, while main raw material ethylene prices only decreased 7.8 percent over the same period, the company said.
MDI prices, however, rose by an average 0.12 German marks per kg for raw MDI and by 0.33 marks per kg for pure MDI.

Borsodchem has an issued share capital of 10.2 billion forints, with the Bank of New York holding 46.7 percent, small investors 31.8 percent, and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development 14.7 percent.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Borsodchem shares closed at 6,040 forints, down 310.
